headline: Geoffrey Hinton warns that the window to set AI safety rules may be only one or two years.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the headline 'self-creation era begins' overstates what Hinton says he does not know.
importance_line: His warning on a short window for AI rules affects policy makers and the public, but the self-improvement figures are company data cited in one paper and he says he does not know how far it has gone.
summary: 36Kr reports, citing an interview by Nayeema Raza, a US journalist and podcast host, that Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel physics laureate and AI pioneer, believes the time left to set up AI rules and safety measures may be only one or two years if progress keeps accelerating. Hinton had reposted, on 3 Oct 2026, a paper by 22 AI researchers on whether automating AI research could trigger an intelligence explosion, and he said he does not know how far that process has already gone.
notes: Reporter chain unclear (36Kr page carries a contributor disclaimer), so 'X reports, citing Y' is used. Organisation of Hinton not in the article. Interview date not stated.
